newsitem.title: RUSSIA: DeBakey sees Yeltsin new man, vigorous leader.
newsitem.headline: DeBakey sees Yeltsin new man, vigorous leader.

text.p: U.S. heart surgeon Michael DeBakey said on Thursday that Boris Yeltsin would be a "vigorous" president and could be back at home in two to three weeks.
"I think he could go back to the Kremlin in two to three weeks," DeBakey said in an interview.
But he added it would take several weeks longer before Yeltsin would be able to work at full strength, following Tuesday's quintuple heart bypass.
DeBakey, a leading U.S. heart surgeon who advised on Yeltsin's surgery, said the president was recovering rapidly and would become a "new man".
"You're going to see a vigorous leader," he said.
DeBakey, 88, said Yeltsin was "pushing" doctors to leave the Cardiology Centre but that the 65-year-old president generally was not a difficult patient.
The Houston, Texas doctor, who performed the world's first successful bypass in 1964, said he had examined Yeltsin's liver and seen no evidence of excessive drinking.
"He's not an alcoholic," DeBakey said and added that Yeltsin would soon be able to drink moderately.
But he said Yeltsin would be told to keep to the low-fat diet he had been on for over a month, for the rest of his life.
He called Yeltsin a motivated patient but said many bypass patients abandoned special diets and regimes as soon as they felt well.

DeBakey said Yeltsin was walking in his hospital room on Thursday morning and would be able to move from the Cardiology Research Centre where he was operated on to the more convenient Central Clinical Hospital on Friday.
